_comment: QUI-1226 — Flux v8 spec for the AGLAIS testnet faucet, a NEW SIBLING app run in parallel
with the live `quipfaucet` during the network reset. Derived from the live dashboard export
2026-09-02; every field below matches it except the ones listed under CHANGED.
Starting point for the dashboard wizard ONLY — the canonical spec is always the export.
CHANGED vs the live quipfaucet:
name/description  -> aglais
repotag           -> built from integration/qui-1226-faucet-aglais (main + !15 + !16)
domains           -> faucet.aglais.quip.network
commands          -> --node-url points at the three AGLAIS bootnodes
UNCHANGED and deliberate: ports/containerPorts 8087, containerData /data, cpu 1 /
ram 2048 / hdd 1, instances 1, staticip false, repoauth "" (the registry is public),
geolocation [acEU, acNA, a!cEU_RU], and the funder key (op-1 = chain sudo).
🔴 WHY A SEPARATE APP: repointing the live quipfaucet's --node-url would take the EXISTING
testnet's faucet offline. The two chains run in parallel, so both need their own.
🔴 THE FUNDER IS THE SAME ACCOUNT ON BOTH CHAINS. Verified 2026-09-02: aglais Sudo::Key is
0xc5c1e685e181d2939fddaf43e61455c0f00a99d2716d59b1f90674e5c0292510 — the same op-1 account
that is sudo on the live testnet. Balances and nonces are per-chain so they cannot collide,
but see the next note, because nothing in the faucet will catch a mis-aimed deploy.
🔴 `--allow-any-chain` IS NOT A CHAIN PIN. It only disables verify_dev_chain(), which refuses
any system_chain not starting with a dev prefix (chain.rs:405-413) — production has to set it.
With it on there is NO genesis or chain-identity check anywhere in the faucet. Combined with a
funder that is sudo on BOTH chains, a wrong --node-url here would silently mint on the wrong
network. The three URLs below are the only thing aiming this app: check them by eye, and after
deploy confirm the running faucet's target rather than assuming.
BEFORE DEPLOYING:
1. repotag digest — build + push, then pin `repo:TAG@sha256:DIGEST`. A bare `repo@sha256:`
is REJECTED by Flux.
2. Enterprise ON — QUIP_FAUCET_FAUCET_KEY is the chain sudo key; empty `enterprise` ships
it as PLAINTEXT env. The toggle generates the blob at submit; it is not a pasted value.
3. Create the faucet.aglais.quip.network CNAME to the new app's FDM name once registered.
TLS is terminated by Flux FDM at the custom domain — there is no certifier/Tarsnap leg
here, unlike the bootnodes.
4. No environmentParameters value may be empty — Flux rejects the whole submission.
REPLACE every <REPLACE:...> before use.
name: quipfaucetaglais
description: Quip aglais testnet faucet: native (SS58 / 0x+64-hex) and EVM (0x+40-hex) funding

compose.name: faucet
compose.description: Rust quip-faucet. Funder is op-1's hybrid account (the chain sudo key); it sudo-mints a dedicated base wallet, funds the /sign pool, and serves /request, /sign, /health over plain HTTP. TLS is terminated by Flux FDM at the custom domain.
environmentParameters: QUIP_FAUCET_FAUCET_KEY=<REPLACE:op-1 mnemonic from Proton Pass — same funder as the live faucet>

enterprise: <REPLACE:NOT a value you paste — flip the Enterprise toggle in the wizard's General tab, which generates the blob at submit. Leaving this off ships the chain sudo key as PLAINTEXT env>
